slides.title: Evolutionary Computation and Genetic Algorithms
The lecture moves from metaphor to executable specification
From atom to species, cells connect three crucial molecules
A one-dimensional sequence helps produce a three-dimensional protein over time
Complementary strands preserve information; codons make the sequence interpretable
Inheritance preserves; crossover and mutation vary; selection changes frequencies
Life and software both store instructions—but the mapping has limits
The metaphor creates five computational commitments
Initialization, evaluation, variation, and replacement form a search loop
The population P(t) is the state that evolves
A problem is not ready until five questions have concrete answers
Maximize a rippled function on [−1, 2]
Six-decimal precision requires at least 22 bits
A chromosome becomes an integer, then a real value in the interval
Create P(0) as 300 random 22-bit candidates
Decode first, evaluate f(x), then bias parent choice
Crossover recombines; mutation introduces local novelty
The complete setup now runs from P(t) to P(t+1)
A nine-city tour exposes why representation changes the operators
Four bits per city are compact—but generic crossover breaks the route
A permutation directly represents visit order
Copy a segment, then fill with the other parent's unused order
Validity is a property students can inspect, not a promise
Power comes from representation–operator fit; so does fragility
Specify one defensible GA, then trade designs for an adversarial audit
Representation determines what evolution can discover
